win_claim.quote: Our experimental results against a number of multi-class problems show that, when the SCUT method is used for pre-processing the data before classification, we obtain highly accurate models that compare favourably to the state-of-the-art.

uncertain: Classifier choice: abstract highlights none; J48 taken as first reported (Table 2, p.5). Paper says SCUT best for Naive Bayes/SMO, SMOTE best for J48/IBk (p.7).

Summary row 'Friedman p-value' is a single test across all 5 methods, not SCUT vs SMOTE; placed in both columns only for reference (p.7).
notes: Proposed method SCUT (SMOTE + EM cluster-based undersampling to class mean). Baselines: SMOTE, RU, CUT (SCUT without SMOTE), Orig. (no sampling). Classifiers: J48, Naive Bayes, SMO, IBk (k=5), WEKA, 10-fold CV. Metrics: G-mean (Tables 2-5, p.5), F-measure (Tables 6-9, p.5-6), AUC (Tables 10-13, p.6); rank summaries Tables 14-16 (p.6); Friedman p-values Table 17 (p.7). Dataset names in results tables are abbreviated (Lympho., Pageblock/Pageblocks/Pageblk, Derma./Derma, Wine). No std reported. All tables are text (verified by rendering pages 4-6). Conclusion (p.8): 'We were not able to establish a clear superiority of one oversampling method over the other.'
